Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB233.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jie’an Jin. Jie'an Jin owns the retained deployment — the message-carrier fellow ruled endless; then his own stamps down the case's every turn: too much labor, losing money invites guilt, just so.

Senses.Explanation: An exasperated cut-off — when will it ever end? — ruled at the root over Linji's coming and going, and stamped on verse-men, word-chewers, tricksters, and echo-chasers from the Song halls to the Qing case-desks. The root sits in Huangbo Xiyun's own question, carried in the tongs-and-hammer record with Feiyin Tongrong's appraisals: Linji, freed by Dayu's grip — your teacher Huangbo, nothing to do with me — returns, and Huangbo sees him and asks: this fellow, coming and going — when will it ever end? only for the grandmotherly heart's sake, the answer; then where have you been, to Dayu at my kind instruction — and what words did Dayu have? the retelling, and the verdict on the tale-bearer: that old fellow Dayu babbles, wait and I'll give him a real beating — say nothing of waiting, hit now! the slap that follows; Dongshan Liangjie, at the old buddha's field where the lords request the teaching, hears the polished couplet — the Dongshan scenery green again, the root-wind of awakening stirred anew — and caps it: when will it ever end?; then questioning stops, words run long and the way runs far; Fenyang Shanzhao, over the case of what Mahakasyapa personally heard — a shout, a bow, a blow — rules the lot: such as these, how could they match the worthies of old; the language-copying crowd, sand-grains and sea-ink, unable to wake on a sudden, ashamed, chasing reflections along the stream, sprouting branches — when will it ever end? not turning the light back, groping the waves of consciousness, the kalpa-stone worn away and still no self-trust: bitter, bitter; the sutra-lord himself named them the pitiable ones; and Dahui, remembering the monk who laughed coldly at his teaching then found the room-door shut — twenty visits in ten days, every trick spent, nothing availing — tells him plainly: no showing of tricks; it must crack and snap outright to stand against birth-and-death; showing tricks — when will that ever end? no need to panic; not won this life, work it the next. Sanyi Mingyu, working the bamboo-comb ban — call it a comb and you touch it, refuse the name and you turn your back; no words, no silence, no woman's bow, no sweeping exit — the ancients split liver and gall, pearl cast into the dark, jade-disc given on a dead-end road, and still, pity on you worthies, you will not probe beneath the notion-root but take it on at the raising — when will it ever end? settled rightly, the mountain-gate moved into the buddha-hall and the kitchen set in the monks' hall, nothing beyond your share; Muyun Tongmen, at the general discourse, asks what the discourse is for: if you merely hear me flap these two skins and you tilt your ears and chase the echo — when will it ever end? you must break through under the very words — Xiangyan Zhixian's old ruling read into it: speech is a cheat, silence is a slander, and above speech and silence there is the affair; and Jie'an Jin, grading the old-woman case line by line — level water does not flow; a beggar's tricks; to poised hands, lost — stamps the relay itself: Chengyi carried it to Zhaozhou — a message-carrier fellow, when will it ever end?; the master's if I saw that stinking old woman I'd question her dumb; and the blow that falls on the carrier who asks why it lands on him: just so.
